first_impression.reaction: I went straight to the FAQ, then the key takeaways. The takeaways have actual sources in them, Smartraveller, UNESCO, the Rome embassy, so this isn't just fluff. Fine, I'll read the legal bit properly and skim the customs.

journey.quote: Smartraveller rates Albania "Exercise a high degree of caution" because of limited healthcare, so guests need travel insurance that covers medical evacuation.
journey.reaction: Good. A wedding blog telling me the downside of the destination up front. That's the opposite of what I expected.

journey.section: Who keeps Albanian wedding customs today
journey.quote: They vary by region, by family and by faith, so treat what follows as a map rather than a rulebook.
journey.reaction: Honest about its limits. I'd rather that than someone pretending there's one correct way.

journey.section: Who keeps Albanian wedding customs today
journey.quote: If you want to see how one couple brought them to an Australian ballroom, read [this Albanian wedding in Melbourne](/real-wedding-a-lavish-albanian-wedding-at-the-manor-of-high-melbourne) from our Real Weddings collection.
journey.reaction: I'd click it, but 'lavish' tells me it'll be photos and adjectives. Show me a real wedding with the actual budget.

journey.quote: Not published: a fixed length of time between the fejesa and the wedding. Families set this themselves.
journey.reaction: Saying what isn't known instead of making up a number. That's what I'd want.

journey.quote: It is often told that the bitter almond and its sweet shell stand for married life, with the sweetness outlasting the rest.
journey.reaction: 'Often told' everywhere in the customs section. At least it's not passed off as fact, but nothing in those bits has a source I could check. Fine for culture, I skimmed it.

journey.section: Marrying legally in Albania as an Australian
journey.quote: This is general information, not legal advice.
journey.reaction: Dated, sourced, with a disclaimer. This is the section I actually came for.

journey.quote: Not published in official sources we could read: the documents, notice period and translation rules Albania's civil status office applies to foreign nationals, or whether a religious ceremony has civil effect on its own.
journey.reaction: Honest, but it's also the exact answer I need. They tell me to go and check it myself, so what does a planner add here?

journey.quote: A fee applies for both the CNI and an apostille.
journey.reaction: How much? It's a government fee, it's published somewhere. Mildly annoying.

journey.section: Travel advice for you and your guests
journey.quote: The page was updated on 16 October 2026 and was still current on 3 November 2026.
journey.reaction: Dates. Exactly what I look for. I can check this myself and it'll match.

journey.quote: Your Advisor is your single point of contact from start to finish, and the fee and inclusions are agreed in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: Better than most. Fee in writing is good. But it doesn't say whether you take a cut from the venue or suppliers, and that's my first question.

unanswered_questions: Do you take commissions or mark-ups from venues and suppliers, or is the Advisor fee the only thing you earn?
Is the Advisor fee flat or a percentage of the budget?
Have you actually run a wedding in Albania, or only Albanian-style weddings in Australia?
What does a planner do about the civil status office steps that I can't do myself by emailing them?

turn_offs_found.quote: It takes a minute and photographs well.
turn_offs_found.why: Small thing, but that's a planner selling me on the look, not a fact. Doesn't bother me much.

would_share_with: My partner, for the legal and Smartraveller section
Parents, for the customs list so we can agree which ones we're doing

cta_reaction.quote: If you would rather have one person holding the plan together, [speak with a Wedded Advisor](/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=article&utm_campaign=albanian-wedding-traditions).
cta_reaction.why: It comes after the evidence, not before, and it's not pushy. I'd click through to see the fee model. If the next page doesn't say whether you take supplier commissions, I'm out.

top_3_changes: Next to the Advisor CTA, state in one line whether Wedded Wonderland takes supplier commissions or mark-ups (or link to a page that does).
In the legal section, say plainly what an Advisor would do about the unpublished civil status steps, so the CTA answers 'what does the fee buy me here'.
If the Melbourne real wedding has budget or guest numbers, mention them in the link sentence; that's the proof I'd click for.

checks.check: Every journey point, turn-off and CTA reaction quotes an exact sentence from 05-draft.md

No invented brand facts; fee model, commissions and Albania track record listed as unanswered questions

open_questions.question: Commission/mark-up transparency is Daniel's main enquiry blocker; is a one-line fee-model statement near the CTA in scope for this post, or deferred with business details?
